title: Mixed-catalog request intent, revision 2: source review

binding.r2Change: four single-$ delimiters to $$ in the two staff_list functions only

sound.catalog: full viewer-scoped master scan via existing reader and pathway authorities, fail-closed on partial scan; baseline 420 products, one variant each; excludes only non-merchandise (2) and coming-soon/planned (none at baseline); clinical care-pathway (244) requestable without price; held/restricted requestable with restriction shown and stored; families, workflow modes and display states match baseline
sound.ownerIsolation: owner only from authenticated viewer (member auth user ID; Early Access customer ref + session hash); email never establishes ownership; recovery requires same owner
sound.minimumData: contact, dated acknowledgments, exact lines; no notes/documents/medical answers/payment facts; closed key sets in TS and SQL; browser keeps only an attempt marker under the existing sign-out sweep prefix
sound.atomicity: single security-definer insert on (owner, attempt) on conflict do nothing then committed-winner read; changed facts conflict; lines and audit together or nothing; service looks up attempt before standing/catalog/legal so a saved attempt always replays
sound.receipt: saved only after a validated receipt; reference derived from stored ID; whitelisted pending-only fields
sound.staffAuthorization: app: exact enabled Care capability + care:administer; DB: active clinical_admin assignment + approved enabled Care row; service_role-only functions; private schema with no table grants, forced RLS, no policies; actor from verified principal; no direct Data API path
sound.baselineParity: billing copied from shipping when same; 200 lines, no duplicates, per-item max 100 match SQL; SHA-256 hex hasher fits 64-hex checks; Care subjectId is auth user ID; care tables have the used columns; client imports exist; catalog strings within 300 chars

requiredCorrection.problem: every non-OK response becomes 'unconfirmed'; form shows the recovery notice and locks editing; reload leaves only the check-earlier-request screen; first-POST 400/401/403/429 means the server refused before any write, and retrying the same frozen attempt cannot succeed for deterministic refusals, so the customer is stuck and the guidance is not truthful
requiredCorrection.fix: expose HTTP status; on the first POST of an attempt treat 400/401/403/429 as not saved with cause-specific guidance, clear the marker and allow edit/resubmit under a fresh attempt; keep 409, every 5xx, network failures, malformed bodies and any refusal on a retry as uncertain; add written tests for both branches
requiredCorrection.scope: client only; not a security change

recommended: rpc-repository maps check violation 23514 and request_intent_invalid 22023 (rolled back) to a definite invalid-request code instead of 503 uncertain
SQL contact cap 6000 bytes can be below TS-valid maximum multibyte text; raise it or bound it in TS
billing address collected for an unapproved request via the reused contract; defensible for follow-up, not needed for intent
integrationBlockers: Care enablement: staff readback needs the Care capability enabled and approved, CARE_ENABLED and CARE_ENABLE_APPROVED, and an active clinical_admin assignment; baseline records Care hard-disabled in production; enabling opens all /api/care; requires Samuel's explicit production decision or a separately reviewed change to an existing staff authority; no authority created here
Care tables come from supabase/care-access-foundation.sql outside migrations; rehearsal and registration must account for it

disposable DB rehearsal before registration: role-setting check inside security-definer functions admits service_role via PostgREST and refuses others; forced RLS without policies works for the owner (bypass rights); insert-or-replay under concurrency; TS-SQL parity; immutability; staff guards
migration placement and registration, then the separate mount/guard/manifest packet for existing customer and staff shells, each with its own review and custody
runtime qualification and release including the browser journey for save, retry, recovery, refusal and staff readback; no notification path, staff must poll the queue
